accuracy.evidence: Definition f̄ = (1/(b − a)) ∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx as in A level/Further Maths texts and the OpenStax Calculus Vol. 1 section on the mean value theorem for integrals. Every number recomputed: ∫₀³ x² dx = 9 so f̄ = 3; hill above and gaps below the line both equal 2√3 ≈ 3.46 at h = 3 (closed forms coded and checked); midpoint sample means 2.25, 2.8125, 2.953, 2.988, 2.997, 2.9993 (3 − 0.75/n²); T = 14 − 6cos(πt/12) gives (1/12)∫₆¹⁸ T dt = 14 + 12/π ≈ 17.82 with T(6) = T(18) = 14; c = √3; sin x averages 2/π on [0, π/2] and [0, π] and 0 on [0, 2π]; challenge answers 3, 5, e − 1, 2/π, 4/3 and 15 m/s checked by hand.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the slips teachers and examiners report for this topic: forgetting to divide by b − a (answers 9, 10, 8/3, 2, e), averaging the end values (4.5, (1 + e)/2, and the temperature window whose ends are both 14 °C), using f at the midpoint (2.25, 1, v(5)), dividing by b instead of b − a (10/3 for 2x + 1 on [1, 3]), and ignoring negative signed area (sin x over a full period).

lab_distinct.evidence: Every activity uses this topic's own mechanism: levelling a line so the area above the curve fills the gaps below it, a sample mean converging to the integral mean, an average over a sliding time window, locating c with f(c) = f̄, and signed-area cancellation. No other flagship has a levelling line or a time-window average; the 6-token shingle gate passed against all flag_*.js labs, including the arc-length and gradient-function labs.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers f̄ = 3 as the level line before the formula is named, then sees the same 3 arise as the limit of the mean of data, applies it in context (the 6 am–6 pm temperature), meets the mean value theorem for integrals by sliding c and finding √3 rather than the midpoint, and finally sees signed area cancel. The done messages confirm each discovery in words.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab then disproves: 4.5 (mean of end values) or 2.25 (midpoint value) for x² on [0, 3]; sample means settling on 4.5; 14 °C (mean of the two end values) or 20 °C (the maximum) for the daytime temperature; and 2/π instead of 0 for sin x over [0, 2π].

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with six distinct m= messages that name the slip: integral without dividing, value at the right end mistaken for the answer, end-value averaging works only for straight lines, dividing by b instead of b − a, full-period 0 confused with [0, π], and f at the midpoint is not the average.

readability.evidence: Learner text reads at FK 4.7 and adult text at FK 8.1, within the learner limits (6.5 and 9.5). Sentences are short; the formula is introduced as 'add up with the integral, divide by the width' before the notation. Canvas labels are one line each and use standard notation (f̄, ∫ₐᵇ, b − a).

no_filler.evidence: Passes the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Each kid paragraph adds a new idea (mean of a list → integral version, worked example, levelling picture, signed area); adult paragraphs cover definition and Riemann-sum link, geometry and the mean value theorem, the named mistakes, and contexts plus what the lab does.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots of all six steps in dark and light, before and after Show me: the plot stacks above the readout panel, tick labels are readable, the temperature handles were moved onto the curve after the first shots showed them hiding the 6 and 18 tick labels, and the control buttons wrap without clipping. The challenge buttons fit on one row.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task completes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, the challenge appears, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes and there are no console errors. Every drag has a button route (line up/down, more/fewer samples, start/end ±1 h, c ± 0.05, b = π/2, π, 2π) and the canvas aria-label reports the current value and what it means after each move.
